public_rationale: OpenAI's prepublication tests support a meaningful factual-reliability concern in models available through ChatGPT. They do not reproduce the claimed cross-context nationality inconsistency, and factual errors alone cannot establish the absence of an internal model. The architectural component remains unsettled, so the combined claim cannot receive a supported verdict.
limitations: PersonQA is a targeted factuality evaluation, not an estimate of error rates across all ChatGPT use.
The evidence does not identify the configuration used in Marcus's anecdote.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: ChatGPT cannot reliably use factual information like Wikipedia's and has no explicit, stable internal world model.

statement.excerpt: But ChatGPT can’t leverage that kind of information reliably, and doesn’t have its own an explicit, stable, internal model.
statement.document_title: Generative AI’s crippling and widespread failure to induce robust models of the world

from_speaker: can’t leverage that kind of information reliably
doesn’t have its own an explicit, stable, internal model
One day it may tell you Shearer is British, another day that he is American
our_interpretation: The plain reading has two components: unreliable use of well-documented factual information and absence of an explicit, stable internal representation.
Reliability means ordinarily dependable factual answers across reasonable variations in context. It does not mean that every answer must be correct.
The reference to Wikipedia concerns information available for learning; it does not establish that a particular response used browsing or retrieved the relevant page.

The target is ChatGPT configurations relevant at publication, assessed using the latest applicable public evaluations. Earlier tests are eligible when their configuration remains relevant; there is no June-only boundary.
criteria.support_condition: Applicable tests show recurring factual errors or contradictions across reasonable contexts, and direct architectural or representation evidence establishes the absence of the claimed stable internal model.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Applicable tests demonstrate dependable factual use across contexts, or direct evidence establishes the explicit, stable internal representation whose existence is denied. Partial findings must be reported separately.

evidence.excerpt: The o4-mini model underperforms o1 and o3 on our PersonQA evaluation.
evidence.explanation: PersonQA tests publicly available facts about people. Reported hallucination rates were 33% for o3 and 48% for o4-mini, supporting the factual-reliability concern in these tested configurations; the evaluation does not establish absence of internal representations.
The launch announcement establishes that the evaluated model was available in ChatGPT before Marcus's post. It does not establish which model produced his example.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Matched factual-consistency tests of the relevant ChatGPT configuration, together with direct architectural or causal representation evidence addressing the claimed stable internal model.
